question: What is the primary focus of a community diagnosis?

options.A: Treating individual patients in a hospital ward
options.B: Diagnosing rare diseases in laboratory animals
options.C: Inspecting the financial records of a local clinic
options.D: Assessing the health status and needs of an entire population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks at the whole population and its environment rather than focusing on a single sick person. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must a community diagnosis look at factors like housing and clean water?

options.A: These environmental factors directly shape the health outcomes of the population
options.B: Building codes are the legal responsibility of public health nurses
options.C: Hospital administrators require these statistics for annual budgeting
options.D: Doctors use these details to prescribe specific pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health is influenced by social, economic, and environmental conditions, not just medical care alone. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is a main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To provide extra funding for international medical research
options.B: To allocate limited healthcare resources where they are needed most
options.C: To replace the need for individual patient physical examinations
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in private hospitals

explanation: Resources are always limited, so finding the highest priority problems ensures supplies and personnel go where they will do the most good. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: How does a community diagnosis help in measuring the success of a health program?

options.A: It guarantees that all diseases will be completely eradicated
options.B: It establishes baseline data before the program starts
options.C: It stops the community from asking for external financial help
options.D: It automatically cures chronic illnesses within the first month

explanation: You cannot measure progress or improvement later if you do not know what the health situation looked like in the beginning. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a comprehensive community diagnosis?

options.A: A financial audit of local government health clinics
options.B: An in-depth study covering all aspects of health and life in the community
options.C: A quick check of only the children under five years old
options.D: A laboratory test for a single infectious disease

explanation: A comprehensive diagnosis looks at everything from demographics and economics to all available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: A public health team rushes to a village to investigate a sudden outbreak of measles only. What type of assessment are they doing?
explanation: You're getting the hang of it! When we zero in on one specific issue or outbreak instead of looking at the whole community, we call it a problem-oriented approach.

question: What is usually the very first step when preparing to study a community?

options.A: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all school children
options.C: Gaining entry and building trust with local community leaders
options.D: Purchasing expensive medical equipment for the local clinic

explanation: Before collecting data, nurses must respect local protocols and gain the cooperation of community leaders to ensure participation. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important to validate data findings with community members after analysis?

options.A: To confirm that the identified problems truly reflect their lived reality
options.B: To ensure the government tax collectors have accurate income records
options.C: To check if the nurses made spelling mistakes in their notebooks
options.D: To force residents to pay for the cost of the research study

explanation: Community validation ensures that outsiders have not misinterpreted the data and that the people agree on what the real priorities are. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Direct observation of stagnant water behind residential houses
options.B: A brand new questionnaire filled out by household heads today
options.C: Interviews conducted by the nurse with mothers in the market
options.D: Past clinic attendance registers and local census reports

explanation: Secondary data refers to information that has already been collected and recorded by someone else for other purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of using direct observation during a community survey?

options.A: It replaces the need to ever talk to local political leaders
options.B: It eliminates the need for any data analysis or calculations
options.C: It allows the nurse to see actual living and environmental conditions firsthand
options.D: It guarantees that no member of the community will fall sick

explanation: Observation lets nurses witness reality directly without relying on what people say or what old records report. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the purpose of comparing local community health statistics with national standards?

options.A: To prove that national health policies are completely useless
options.B: To eliminate the need for conducting household surveys
options.C: To punish the local health workers for poor performance
options.D: To see where the local health indicators fall behind or exceed standard levels

explanation: Comparing local numbers to national data helps highlight specific areas where the community is suffering more than average. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is data analysis a critical step before planning any healthcare intervention?

options.A: It allows nurses to guess which disease is causing trouble without proof
options.B: It turns raw numbers into clear insights so the real problems become visible
options.C: It ensures that all health funding goes directly into hospital building projects
options.D: It stops community members from expressing their personal opinions

explanation: Without analysis, data remains a confusing pile of numbers that cannot guide effective action. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which criterion is commonly used when setting priorities among several community health problems?

options.A: The color of the pamphlets printed by the health ministry
options.B: The personal preference of the visiting medical doctor
options.C: The distance from the capital city to the village
options.D: The seriousness and fatality rate of the condition

explanation: Problems that cause the most severe illness, disability, or death are usually placed at the top of the priority list. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h7)

question: A village has cases of both common colds and severe childhood malnutrition. Which problem should nurses tackle first?

options.A: Neither, because nurses should wait for the rainy season to pass
options.B: Both equally, because all health complaints carry the exact same weight
options.C: Malnutrition, because it has a much higher risk of permanent harm and death
options.D: Common colds, because they affect every single person in the village

explanation: Great choice! We always prioritize life-threatening and severe conditions like malnutrition over mild illnesses that clear up on their own.

question: What is the main benefit of involving local stakeholders in a community health project?

options.A: It completely removes the need for public health nurses
options.B: It ensures long-term sustainability and local ownership
options.C: It guarantees immediate financial profit for the local clinic
options.D: It stops people from asking questions about project costs

explanation: When people help build and run a program, they care for it and keep it going long after external aid departs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h8)

question: Why do health interventions often collapse after external funding stops?

options.A: The weather in the village suddenly became too harsh
options.B: The community never truly felt ownership of the project
options.C: The local nurses forgot how to write monthly reports
options.D: The national government banned all foreign medical supplies

explanation: If locals are treated as passive recipients rather than active partners, they will not maintain the project once outsiders leave. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in public health projects?

options.A: Monitoring costs a lot of money, while evaluation is completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is continuous tracking, while evaluation measures final outcomes against objectives
options.D: Monitoring focuses on finance, while evaluation focuses entirely on building roads

explanation: Monitoring happens all through the project to keep things on track, whereas evaluation looks back to see if goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)

question: Why is the evaluation phase considered important for future public health work?

options.A: It provides lessons learned that improve future health planning and interventions
options.B: It prevents community members from complaining to political leaders
options.C: It automatically secures a larger budget for the following year
options.D: It proves that nurses never make mistakes during fieldwork

explanation: Evaluating past successes and failures shows what works best, guiding better decisions for the next community health cycle. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h9)
